_rule: ARC-07-S07. THE list of cloud-sync paths, satisfied by three implementations: the server's detectCloudSync() in src/store/paths.ts, the bootstrap's stdlib re-implementation in tools/snowarch/lib/cloud-sync.mjs (ARC-06-S05, for a checkout that has never run npm ci), and the doctor's E-25 (ARC-08-S03). Three tables that merely look alike would drift; one fixture cannot.
_shape: synced[]: { path, provider, root, why } — every one of these MUST be detected, with that provider. quiet[]: { path, why } — every one of these MUST be null. env[]: { path, set: {VAR: value}, provider, root, why } — the Windows environment roots, which no path pattern can catch. icloudFolders[]: { path, home, platform, euid, keys, links, missing, folder, asked, why } — ARC-09-C305, macOS only, read by detectIcloudFolders() and the engine's E-34 and B01 and NOT by detectCloudSync(): the folders carry no marker in their path, so the rule also needs the Finder setting. keys{}: Finder preference -> the raw stdout of `defaults read`, a key that is absent is a reader that failed. links{}: path -> target of a symbolic link. missing[]: paths that are not there. folder: the folder that is reported, or null. asked[]: the Finder keys the reader must be asked for, in order, which is also how a row says that the reader was NOT asked.
_paths: Synthetic. No path here exists on any machine, and none is derived from a real user's home directory.

synced.why: AC 3. macOS mounts every vendor under ~/Library/CloudStorage/<Provider>-<tenant>.
AC 3. How macOS spells iCloud on disk, and no user calls it that.
AC 3. The tenant is suffixed onto the folder name with a spaced hyphen.
AC 3. The outer folder matches first.
A vendor the table does not name is still synchronised; the honest answer names the mount.
ARC-04-S02 criterion 8, kept: the plain consumer folder.
ARC-06-S05's case: the vendor IS named, so the mount is not the answer.

quiet.why: AC 3. The Windows global store is not synced by default — the WARN offers it as the alternative.
ARC-04-S02 criterion 8: the word inside a longer name is not a folder boundary.

env.why: Known Folder Move: the enterprise policy redirects Documents into OneDrive and the word OneDrive appears nowhere in the path. %OneDrive% is the only detector there is.
The commercial client sets its own variable.
The variable is set but this path is not under it — a set variable is not a blanket yes.

icloudFolders.why: Documents is in iCloud Drive and the path says nothing of it: the case the path rules cannot see.
The same for Desktop, with its own key.
Anywhere below the folder, not only directly in it.
The default volume is case-insensitive, so a path typed in lower case is the same folder; the report names the folder as macOS does.
A link into Documents is a path into Documents: the real path is matched, as detectCloudSync does for the named vendors.
A home folder that is itself a link, as on managed machines: both sides are resolved before they are compared.
Both folders on: only the key of the folder the checkout is in is asked, once.
Sync off: macOS makes a NEW local Desktop when the setting is turned off, so being on the Desktop proves nothing.
The key is absent (defaults exits 1): never set, or renamed by a later macOS. That is silence, the way it was before this rule.
Desktop is on and Documents is off: the key of THAT folder decides, not the other one.
Documents is on and Desktop is off: the same, the other way.
Only exactly 1 is ON: any other word, however true it sounds, is OFF.
Documents is a link to somewhere else: who manages the target is not known, so nothing is asked and nothing is said. A documented limit.
The same for a Desktop that is a link.
The folder is not there (deleted), so it is not a folder iCloud manages.
Segments of <home>/Documents, not a substring: Documents2 is another folder.
And not a suffix either.
A folder called Documents on another volume is not the home folder's.
Another account's Documents: its setting is not this account's to read.
Elsewhere in the home folder with both keys on: a path that misses never reaches the reader.
HOME is overridden, so the home folder the doctor was given is not the account's: a real hit under the account's home is missed. Accepted, and it is why tests inject the reader.
Linux has no Desktop & Documents Folders: not asked, whatever the key says.
Neither has Windows (Known Folder Move is the %OneDrive% rows above).
As root the reader would read root's preferences, not the user's: not asked (ARC-09-C303).
No home folder given: nothing to compare with, nothing asked.
